Fix EXC_BAD_ACCESS when invoking brew with a nil return block

Clicking Pin crashed: pinSelectedFormula: calls pinFormula:withReturnBlock:
with a nil block, but performAsyncBrewCommandWithArguments: invoked that block
unconditionally — at the DEBUG warning (fires before the task runs) and at the
task-done message. Calling a NULL block is an EXC_BAD_ACCESS. Every prior
caller (install/uninstall/tap/…) always passed a non-nil block, so this latent
bug only surfaced now that pin/unpin legitimately pass nil.

- Route both interface block invocations through a new nil-guarding helper
  invokeOutputBlock:withString:.
- Also guard BPTask's streaming callback (self.updateBlock) against a nil block
  — it's normally gated by shouldUsePartialUpdates, but a nil could still race
  in if cleanup clears updateBlock while a dispatched output block is pending.

Regression test: invokeOutputBlock: with a nil block must be a safe no-op
(without the guard this crashes the test process) and still delivers the
string to a non-nil block. Extracted the helper specifically so this is
unit-testable without spawning a real brew subprocess.

Verified: Debug build 0 warnings, 59 unit tests green (57 + 2).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
